mechanism: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) acts as a cofactor for aromatic amino acid decarboxylase, converting levodopa to dopamine peripherally and reducing CNS bioavailability, thereby decreasing therapeutic efficacy of levodopa in Parkinson's disease.
action: Avoid high-dose vitamin B6 supplementation; carbidopa-levodopa formulations already contain carbidopa to inhibit peripheral conversion, but supplemental B6 can overcome this effect and reduce therapeutic benefit.
